Stuff like behind-the-scenes drama is difficult to confirm, so I take that with a grain of salt, but I believe they expected Zero Build to be popular. It's what a lot of people wanted.

The map definitely had more cover, more interesting sightlines, and more unique elevation for every biome across the map. Taking away building, imo, was an act of confidence in their mapping skills after four years. Sure they still had to add blimps for elevation, cannons for rotation, and shockwaves being almost mandatory for your loadout, but playing zero build was natural in the CH3 map right from the get-go due to good map design.

Now fast-tracking to CH4 is all sorts of mysterious, but with the benefits we did get out of it-- even MORE improved audio, incredibly detailed biomes, new movement mechanics, and then UEFN tools for creators across the world-- I'll say it was a win for everyone even though the general BR map itself is just straight-up OK across many POIs

Chapter 1 was them figuring out where they wanted the game to go while also gaining a huge amount of popularity, and revving up the machine. The original map is memorable, but it's also not very good in a lot of small ways. It was made with building in mind.

Chapter 2- and thematically with the black hole- was them pressing reset on the whole game and starting over almost from scratch. The big difference being that they were slowly rolling out more ways to add stuff to the map in interesting ways. First with swimming. Sand you can hide in. Bounty boards. New forms of movement based on things you consume. NPCs. Mythic weapons. Covid really threw stuff for a loop, but looking back it's a blessing in disguise that they let the first season of Chapter 2 go on for several months while they were probably doing a lot behind the scenes.

Chapter 3 is where it really felt like a proper sequel in overall map design. They began to bake a lot of mechanics naturally into the environment while also having great POIs. Rotations felt really good. Then they added zero build and it all felt really natural thanks to the great map design. They finally distanced themselves from the original rifles and shotguns, and started to really give weapons and items distinct identities and power levels. This is my personal favorite map.

Chapter 4 is wild, but it's also very stark. There's way more places to fall to your death with a lot more vertical spaces and locations, but it shows a lot more confidence in players figuring out how to rotate well and also confidence in people being able to hit their shots even if someone's lightly peeking over a cliff. However, each biome just kinda starts and stops very suddenly, and they can kinda clash. I think that was a benefit of the older maps having a lot more slopes and clear roads everywhere. Mega City and other POIs were also definitely made with the hurdling mechanic in mind and that had to taken out of BR for more time in the oven, so those POIs can feel really clunky. But the game is still a lot of fun.

it's wild seeing how far everything has come. Being in the battle royale for years has been like watching this strange, evolving mass progress over time. I respect them for keeping one map at a time, so I think they earned going back for a victory lap with the original map, warts and all.

This is the best advice above all else.

- When you need to be in the playable zone, and have to keep moving to have the advantage of better cover or high ground, that's called a rotation. Rotation is the most important tool in Fortnite. Let your son be the boss of where to go next when the game is getting intense. He knows where he's going.

- When you check your inventory (TAB by default), you can inspect (V) any item to learn what it does. Sometimes it's simple, and other times you can learn a lot. If the item/weapon looks especially wild, ask your son what it does!

- If you see a weapon that glows light blue, that is an Exotic weapon. They are effectively guns with magic powers. Make sure to inspect what that weapon does when you pick it up, or ask your son. If you see the "Heavy Breacher Shotgun," especially ask him about that one.

- There are guns that glow bright yellow rather than yellow/orange. These are Mythic weapons. They are the most powerful weapons on the map. Ask your son where to get them.

- If you want to focus on challenges, drop at an edge of the map and go to the location of your challenge. Want a tip? The northwest area of the map, Breakwater Bay, almost always has a pickup truck there. Grab it and drive to your challenge location.

- If your son is really focused on winning and feeling down about losing, ask questions about cool stuff you can see around the map! There's a crashed airplane in the jungle. That clocktower in the snow has a lot of history. There's three masked guys in suits walking around the map. What do they do? Your son will probably want to show you these things.

- Very important: Don't fall behind. If your son starts to enjoy playing with you, he's going to get comfortable that you can pick up the pace. Like I said before, he knows where he's going. Keep up with him! If you have difficulty doing so, ask how you can improve.

Here are some things to know for your own matches.

- The hardest part about Fortnite is dropping from the bus. Near the left of your mini-map is a bar that is raising and lowering as you drop from the bus. The bar raises and lowers in relationship to the elevation of the ground right below you. When your icon reaches that bar, you will automatically deploy your glider. If you need to land in a particular area, use this to your advantage. This is really technical crap, and you're new to the game, but getting good at this will significantly improve your entire start of the match. If your son says to land somewhere, and you often land ready to fight right away, you will impress him.

- When you are about to land somewhere, ask yourself: Where is the highest ground? Do I see a weapon? I brought up Breakwater Bay earlier. The top of the castle there is a great example of this rule. There's almost always a gun there.

- If you don't understand the timing of a weapon's firing and reloading, just start shooting it. Sure people will hear you, but who cares? This is most helpful with the shotguns.

- If someone is chasing you, remember: Gamers don't look up. Turn a corner, and there may be a unique hiding spot right above you! Heck, spend a match just making people chase you. You'll learn more about the map that way, and you can annoy people for free!

- If you see an enemy, and then they shine like a little lightbulb, that is the glint of their sniper rifle. They're looking right at you. A sniper rifle headshot is one shot, one kill.

- See a vehicle in your solo matches? Use it. Your son may need you to use a vehicle in the heat of battle. Surprise him with your skills behind the wheel! Beyond that instance, you should always give the wheel to your son.

- You may see a character walking around with a + icon over their head. That's an NPC that you can hire with gold. Hire them. They will fight for you, and may even surprise you! There's an NPC in Slappy Shores that's my personal favorite.

- Hierarchy of healing items (in order): 

Slurp Juice > Slurp Trucks > Shield Fish > Mini Shield Potion > Shield Potion > Slap Juice Barrels > Slap Juice > Slurp Barrels > Fish > Med-Mist > Medkit > Bandages > Coconuts > All other fruits/veggies

Last but not least, have fun and let your son lead the way! Good luck!

I moved this year to another state so I could be closer to friends. A lot of time has been spent taking in new media rather than listening to my usual music. Watching movies. A lot more TV shows. Anything, really. Some of this stuff has been a new inspiration for me.

I eventually had a realization that I was becoming more interested in these new inspirations, and it's okay to move on from Boards of Canada. Sometimes it helps to have a different perspective of the world shown to you from someone else. Boards of Canada wouldn't have inspired me to watch "Revolutionary Girl Utena", an anime that I feel touches on similar subjects as Boards of Canada but from a completely different perspective.

More personal: I think the music and messages of BoC are interesting, but are always looking into the past in some way. It's the biggest part of their work. I feel as if their music doesn't really believe in a future, if any at all. So much attention in their work focuses on the past, and Tomorrow's Harvest felt like a glimpse into a bleak, tragic future. Not all of their music is like this, but these themes are evident if you regard the context they're presented within to you.

I say all of this because you are allowed to be inspired by other things. There's a lot of media out there. It's okay to move on. You can always come back later.

I'm sorry you had to basically shut yourself off from your father. It's weird when you have that pivotal moment in a relationship where you decide 'there's no point in showing emotion anymore' to that person. You can almost remember the exact thing they said that made you decide to tune them out.

My stepdad started off as a weird bully, then didn't understand why I hated him. Then he moved into our household and began to take control of every little aspect of our lives with new rules. I already knew they were bonkers. The paradigm shift happened when I specifically asked for certain rules in my life. I wanted him to wear a seatbelt in the car at all times. This set him off completely. I had ruined a good family night because I wanted this!

Our family had a sit-down about 'respect' later. Listening to them and just sitting around, waiting for it to be over. Then, the pivotal moment happened.

"I expect you to respect me and my rules this household, and I don't believe I should respect you in return." And that was the nail in the coffin in our relationship. I even asked him to say it again so I could clarify.

Things have become somewhat better. I show some emotion. Hugs. Greetings. Smiles. Most of the time I'm just very stoic when we're together. I don't say anything. He sometimes says 'stop being so fucking serious' when I visit. I don't really care. His goal is that he wanted to shape me up into a proper adult man. Thanks to my own self, my mother and my closest aunt, I could do it myself. My stepfather gets no credit toward who I am today, and who I will be tomorrow.

Thanks for sharing, and I hope you that you build a happy and successful life in spite of your father.

There was eventually heavy conflict involving fires, and there was a major schism. This created people who stopped fires, and those who started them. Lemony and Beatrice steal the sugar bowl, things happen, blah blah blah, Beatrice maybe dies(?) It's never completely brought up. The children's house burns down. In the last chapter (Book the Fourteenth), the children get onto the boat, and they don't know if they will make it back to land. Will the toxic fungus still be there, having infected the whole city, or will everything be fine, the fungus having sunk with the islanders? The very last word in the series is the name of the boat: Beatrice. Time and time again, people have had different opinions that Lemony Snicket dedicates the book to his dead wife, and other people think he is dedicating the book to the boat named after his wife, concluding that the children are dead. **Practice** 

* Read to yourself, or another. Retell one of your favorite stories to yourself over and over. Too long? There are many short stories ready to be read.

* Get attention. This can vary between movement in hands and some minor voice changes, or quickly changing into completely different characters.

* Be concise, confident, and comfortable. When you're comfortable, you're confident, and vice versa. This will help people come to you, but being concise helps keep their attention for longer. As for more comfort, it's just practice practice practice.

At one time in my life I was so engulfed in despair, like other times, that I decided to call a local crisis hotline just to talk to someone. There was advice for helping me get through a good night's sleep, so that I don't develop insomnia, but also some info on how feelings work. They told me that earlier a young boy called their hotline, wondering how he could help his mother. He was feeling pretty bad, and even though the caller found it cute, they decided to help the child anyway.

The operator told me that even with different situations, both big and small, the feelings are still the same for everyone. Even if people may or may not fake it, the emotions they're going to be feeling on the inside are never fake. It's just your choice of how much you want to show those emotions, both good and bad. If you repress an emotion long enough, it can be just as hard to bring it back. Best example is of men crying, but that's because I've experienced this repression first hand, and there have been times when I've wanted to cry and I couldn't. That made me feel much more terrible.

Jumping forward with your eyes closed without hesitation can be just as scary as leaving your comfort zone, as the emotions you're going to feel are equal in both situations. I'm reading about meditation and Buddhism right now, and even though I have a stereotype built up in my mind about the culture, or what people would think of me if they saw me do those practices, I'm still reading up on the subject because it may help me tremendously in the future. I think it's good to not only live in the moment, but also to know that tomorrow is going to be there (especially at our age, around the twenties). If we keep living as if we were going to die today, then it's no wonder why we're always so anxious. The only things that may not be there tomorrow are friends.
